blurb: Elegant British bird dog with a white, flecked belton coat and silky feathering
description: The English Setter is a medium-sized British gun dog with a silky white coat flecked with colour, known as belton, and a gentle, people-oriented temperament.
answer: The English Setter is a medium-sized gun dog from Britain, bred to find and point game birds such as quail, pheasant and grouse. Its mainly white coat is flecked with colour, a pattern called belton. The breed standard sums up its character as a Gentleman by Nature.

body: Setting dogs were trained bird dogs in England more than 400 years ago, and evidence suggests the breed arose from crosses of the Spanish Pointer, large Water Spaniel and English Springer Spaniel. The modern breed owes its look to Edward Laverack (1800–1877) and Richard Purcell Llewellin, whose strains are still referred to as Laverack and Llewellin Setters. The first dog registered by the American Kennel Club was an English Setter named Adonis. In the UK the breed has been listed among Vulnerable Native Breeds.

It is an elegant dog standing about 61 to 68 cm, with a slightly domed head, dark eyes and a tail reaching the hock. The flat, silky coat has long feathering on the ears, chest, legs, belly and tail. Belton colours are blue, orange, lemon and liver belton, plus tricolour. Field-bred dogs are usually finer, with less coat and more distinct spotting, than show dogs.

The breed is commonly described as gentle, intensely friendly and good-natured, and particularly happy with children, though field lines can be strong-willed and mischievous. It is described as intelligent but not always easy to train, as bird scent distracts it outdoors. It is sensitive to criticism, so reward-based training is usually recommended.

English Setters are active dogs, and up to two hours of exercise a day is recommended, though they tend to be calm indoors. The long show coat needs regular grooming; the shorter field coat needs less.

A 2024 UK study found a life expectancy of 13.1 years. Conditions reported in the breed include congenital deafness, which one 2010 study found in 12.4% of dogs tested, autoimmune thyroiditis, hypothyroidism, elbow dysplasia, allergies and atopic dermatitis.

faq.q: Are English Setters good with children?
faq.a: The breed is commonly described as intensely friendly and particularly happy with children.
A Llewellin Setter is an English Setter descended from the 19th-century strain of breeder Richard Purcell Llewellin, not a separate breed.

faq.q: Is the English Setter recognised by the FCI?
faq.a: Yes. It is FCI breed number 2 in Group 7, Pointing Dogs.
